q.t: In a right triangle, the side opposite θ is 3, the side next to θ is 4 and the hypotenuse is 5. Find sin θ.
q.e: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse.

q.t: If sin θ = 5/13, find cos θ (θ acute).
q.e: Opposite 5, hypotenuse 13, so adjacent = √(169 − 25) = 12; cos θ = 12/13.

q.t: sec θ is the reciprocal of…
q.e: sec θ = hypotenuse ÷ adjacent, which is cos θ turned upside down.

q.t: If cosec θ = 2, find sin θ.
q.e: sin θ is the reciprocal of cosec θ.

q.t: Find sin 30°.
q.e: Half of an equilateral triangle of side 2 has hypotenuse 2 and side 1 opposite 30°.

q.t: Find sin 60°.
q.e: In the half-equilateral triangle (1, √3, 2), the side opposite 60° is √3.

q.t: What is tan 90°?
q.e: tan 90° = sin 90°/cos 90° = 1/0, and we cannot divide by zero.

q.t: Find tan 30°.
q.e: In the (1, √3, 2) triangle, opposite 30° is 1 and adjacent is √3.

q.t: 1 + tan² θ equals…
q.e: Divide sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 by cos² θ.

q.t: Find sec² θ − tan² θ.
q.e: Rearrange 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ.

q.t: If tan θ = 8/15, find sin θ.
q.e: Opposite 8, adjacent 15, so hypotenuse = √(64 + 225) = 17.

q.t: If sin A = 3/5, find tan A + sec A.
q.e: Adjacent = 4: tan A = 3/4, sec A = 5/4, total 8/4.

q.t: If 3 tan θ = 4, find (4 sin θ − cos θ)/(4 sin θ + cos θ).
Can sin θ = 4/3 for some angle θ?
o: No — sin θ can never be more than 1
q.e: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, and the hypotenuse is the longest side.

q.t: Find 3 tan² 45° − sin² 60° + cos² 30°.
If tan 2A = √3 (2A acute), find A in degrees.
ΔABC is right-angled at B with ∠A = 30° and AC = 20 cm. Find BC.
q.e: BC is opposite 30°: BC = AC sin 30° = 20 × 1/2.

q.t: If sec θ + tan θ = 4, find sec θ − tan θ.
q.e: (sec θ + tan θ)(sec θ − tan θ) = sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, so it is 1/4.

q.t: Simplify (1 + cot² A)(1 − cos A)(1 + cos A).
q.e: cosec² A × (1 − cos² A) = cosec² A × sin² A.

q.t: If tan θ + cot θ = 2, find tan² θ + cot² θ.
q.e: Square: tan² θ + cot² θ + 2 tan θ cot θ = 4, and tan θ cot θ = 1.

q.t: If sin θ = 5/13, find (sec θ + tan θ)/(sec θ − tan θ).
If tan θ = 3/2, find (3 sin θ − 2 cos θ)/(3 sin θ + 2 cos θ).
q.e: Divide top and bottom by cos θ: (3 tan θ − 2)/(3 tan θ + 2) = (4.5 − 2)/(4.5 + 2) = 2.5/6.5.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at B with AB = 12 cm and sin A = 5/13. Find its perimeter.
q.e: BC/AC = 5/13 with AB = 12 means the 5–12–13 triangle: BC = 5, AC = 13.

q.t: If sin(2θ − 10°) = cos 60° (θ acute), find θ in degrees.
If cos(A − B) = √3/2 and sin(A + B) = 1, find A in degrees.
A ladder makes 60° with the ground and its foot is 2.5 m from the wall. Find the ladder’s length.
q.e: cos 60° = foot distance ÷ ladder: 2.5 ÷ 1/2.

q.t: Find 4 cos³ 30° − 3 cos 30°.
If sin θ + cos θ = 7/5, find sin θ cos θ.
q.e: Square: 1 + 2 sin θ cos θ = 49/25, so 2 sin θ cos θ = 24/25.

q.t: If sin θ + cos θ = 7/5 and sin θ > cos θ, find sin θ − cos θ.
q.e: (sin θ − cos θ)² = 1 − 2 sin θ cos θ = 1 − 24/25 = 1/25.

q.t: (tan θ + sec θ − 1)/(tan θ − sec θ + 1) equals…
q.e: Replace the 1 on top by sec² θ − tan² θ, factor out (sec θ + tan θ), and the rest cancels.

q.t: If tan θ = 8/15, find (1 − sin θ + cos θ)/(1 + sin θ + cos θ).
If 5 sin² θ + 3 cos² θ = 4 (θ acute), find tan θ.
q.e: Write 3 cos² θ = 3 − 3 sin² θ: 2 sin² θ + 3 = 4, so sin² θ = 1/2 and θ = 45°.

q.t: ΔABC is right-angled at B with AC + AB = 9 cm and BC = 3 cm. Find sec A + tan A.
q.e: AC² − AB² = 9, so (AC − AB) × 9 = 9 and AC − AB = 1: AC = 5, AB = 4. sec A = 5/4, tan A = 3/4.

q.t: If sin(A + B) = 1 and cos(A − 2B) = 1 (A, B acute), find A in degrees.
Find (sec² 45° + cot² 60° + 3 tan² 30°)/(cosec² 30° − tan² 60°).
If sin(A − B) = 1/2 and cos(A + B) = 0 (A, B acute), find B in degrees.
q.e: A − B = 30° and A + B = 90°: subtract to get 2B = 60°.

q.t: If cosec θ − sin θ = l and sec θ − cos θ = m, find l²m²(l² + m² + 3).
q.e: l = cos² θ/sin θ and m = sin² θ/cos θ, so lm = sin θ cos θ and l² + m² + 3 = 1/(sin² θ cos² θ).

q.t: If 4 sin θ + 3 cos θ = 3, find 3 sin θ − 4 cos θ.
If sec θ + tan θ = 3 (θ acute), find sin θ.
q.e: sec θ − tan θ = 1/3. So sec θ = 5/3, tan θ = 4/3, and sin θ = tan θ/sec θ.

q.t: If sin θ + cos θ = p and sec θ + cosec θ = q, then q(p² − 1) equals…
q.e: q = p/(sin θ cos θ) and p² − 1 = 2 sin θ cos θ.
